This guide sets up a resonant-mode calculation for your own model. You need a
`snapshot` with Nets assigned; see [Work with your own model](working-model.qmd).
The [resonance tutorial](../tutorials/resonance-epr/prepare.qmd) walks through the
same steps for a single pad.

Eigenmode runs without any surface films, junction port or EPR request. Add
those only if you need them.

## Set up the modes

```python
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display
from scgsim.palace import EigenmodeSim

sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/xmon-modes"))
sim.set_eigenmode(num_modes=2, target=2e9, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)
sim.set_mesh(refined_mesh_size=5.0, max_mesh_size=300.0)
display(sim.input_summary())
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `num_modes` | How many modes to find. |
| `target` | Target frequency for the mode search, in Hz. |
| `tolerance` | Eigenvalue solver tolerance. |
| `save` | Number of mode fields to save for visualization; `0` saves none. |

Mesh sizes are in micrometres. `set_mesh` also accepts `algorithm_3d`,
`threads`, `surface_threads`, `geometry_order` and `high_order_optimize`; see
the [mesh settings reference](../specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls-110-candidate).
For element order and adaptive refinement, use `sim.set_numerical(...)` as in
the [resonance tutorial](../tutorials/resonance-epr/prepare.qmd#step-1-set-up-the-eigenmode-calculation).
SCGSim sets Palace's `Nonconformal` refinement to false unless you set
`amr_nonconformal=True`.

`input_summary()` shows the model and settings without meshing.

**Boundary.** The vacuum region comes from the plan. Its outer surface is left
unassigned, so Palace treats it as a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC). HFSS
uses a Perfect E boundary by default, so the two solvers can give different
frequencies for the same geometry.

## Add a junction and EPR (optional)

To model a linearized Josephson junction, add an inductive port on an
authored sheet, and request the participation you want reported:

```python
sim.add_port("chip/o_junction_lumped", layer="D0_TOP_M1",
             layout_sheet=True, inductance=10e-9)
sim.set_epr_request(
    surface_interfaces=("MA", "MS", "SA"),
    bulk_domain_ids=None,
    port_names=("chip/o_junction_lumped",),
)
```

Surface participation also needs film parameters from `set_surface_epr`; see
the [resonance tutorial](../tutorials/resonance-epr/prepare.qmd#step-1-set-up-the-eigenmode-calculation)
and the [Xmon Palace example](../tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd). The EPR request
only selects what is reported. It does not remove materials from the model.

Palace reports a *signed* port participation. HFSS reports nonnegative
inductive and capacitive ratios instead. [Energy participation and
loss](../eigenmode-epr.qmd) explains the difference.

## Build the mesh

```python
mesh_path = sim.mesh()
config_path = sim.write_config()
```

`mesh()` builds the conformal mesh with Gmsh. Metal interiors are excluded
from the solution. If you change the geometry or mesh settings afterwards,
call `mesh()` again; if the source model changes, make a new snapshot.

`sim.mesh_summary()` reports element counts and an estimated number of
unknowns for the chosen element order. Palace reports the actual number after
the run.

## Run and read the result

1. Optionally, [inspect the prepared run](solver-observations.qmd).
2. [Run it](execute.qmd).
3. [Read the result](returned-results.qmd).

For each mode, the report gives the frequency, the quality factor Q and, if
requested, participation ratios. Check how the frequency *and* any
participation you use changed over the refinement passes; they can converge
at different rates.

If the model has no loss, Palace reports $Q = +\infty$. The report shows this
as "native-reported infinite Q" and leaves Q-derived values empty. See the
[native Q reference](../specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#native-eigenmode-q).

## Example: Circular Pad LC study {#circular-pad-lc-study}

This example applies the steps above to a circular pad with curved
boundaries. The OrPen SC PDK lesson for it is at revision
[`ecc9062`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/tree/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52):
[source lesson](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/palace_eigenmode.qmd),
[notebook](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/palace_eigenmode.ipynb)
and [result data](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/evidence/README.md).

![The Circular Pad layout on a 1000 µm die. The detail shows the east-side
junction sheet.](../assets/circular-pad-layout.png){#fig-circular-pad-source-layout}

The model is a pad of radius 100 µm with a 20 µm radial gap, on 500 µm silicon
with 0.2 µm aluminium. A 2 µm-wide sheet on the east side carries a 10 nH
junction inductance. The pad's circular edges are exact arcs, which Palace
meshes with second-order geometry.

### Load the component {#select-the-curved-source-cell}

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
Set up the Circular Pad environment:
[Install SCGSim](installation.qmd#env-circular-pad).
:::

```python
import gdsfactory as gf
import orpen_sc_pdk

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
component = gf.get_component(
    "circular_pad_capacitor",
    outer_radius_um=100.0,
    inner_radius_um=0.0,
    gap_um=20.0,
    die_side_um=1000.0,
    junction_width_um=2.0,
)
```

Then build the plan as in [Work with your own model](working-model.qmd). The
component already carries its arcs; the snapshot passes them to Palace.

::: {#native-palace-for-this-curved-uniform-port .callout-important title="This example needs a patched Palace"}
The curved junction port needs a Palace build from
[revision `4e9e1b7`](https://github.com/arfiligol/palace/tree/4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37)
or later, which contains a
[fix for curved port extents](https://github.com/arfiligol/palace/blob/4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37/palace/utils/geodata_impl.cpp).
Other Palace examples do not need it.
:::

The notebook's mesh uses the HXT algorithm, geometry order 2 with one
high-order optimization pass, element order 2 and at most four adaptive
refinement passes. It runs on 8 MPI processes × 1 thread.

The notebook starts with `WORKFLOW_ACTION = "analyze_handoff"`, which needs a
previous run directory that is not published. To run it yourself, choose
`prepare_handoff` or `run` and a new `RUN_ID`.

### Result

Our run finished after four refinement passes with mode 1 at
**5.573 GHz**.

![Mode-1 frequency and Palace error estimate across the refinement
passes.](../assets/circular-pad-frequency-amr.png){#fig-circular-pad-frequency-amr}

This result is **not converged**. The final error estimate is 0.119, against
a requested tolerance of 0.02; Palace stopped because it reached the
four-pass limit. The log also shows linear-solver (PCG) convergence warnings
in postprocessing. Use more refinement passes before relying on the
frequency.

The junction participation is −0.995. The minus sign is Palace's sign
convention for port participation, not negative energy. The surface films use
literature values, so the surface-loss figures are illustrations, not a
prediction of this device's Q or $T_1$.

::: {.callout-note title="How the curved port is modelled"}
The lumped port uses one fixed direction (+x) and an equivalent width
$w = A/l$, where $A$ is the port area and $l$ its length along that
direction. This is an approximation of the voltage across a curved gap.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Run details" collapse="true"}
The final mesh had 114 197 tetrahedra and 846 008 unknowns. The run used
SCGSim `1.1.0rc1` at
[`2eed1eb`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/tree/2eed1eb4a9bcc7b1b020feb4953d5ed27e7d7b71)
and Palace `4e9e1b7`. The
[run manifest](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/evidence/run_set.json)
lists all inputs.
:::
